question.worked_solution:
First, we convert the given probability into a cumulative probability using the complement:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le -1.1) & =1-P(X>-1.1) \\  & =1-0.2578 \\  & =0.7422\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le -1.1) & =0.7422 \\ P(Z\le \frac{-1.1+3.7}{\sigma }) & =0.7422 \\ Φ(\frac{2.6}{\sigma }) & =0.7422 \\ \frac{2.6}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7422)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.65)=0.7422\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7422)=0.65.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2.6}{\sigma } & =0.65 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{2.6}{0.65} \\ \sigma  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2}={4}^{2}=16.\end{aligned}
$$
